newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market $68, light -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market $68, light -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Wednesday sold at $68.00 per cwt in light volume, unchanged from heavy trading on Tuesday, feedlot sources said.
In the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma about 6,500 head traded, bringing the weekly movement near 85,000. Several feedlot sources said Panhandle showlists were close to sold out.
Kansas sales were estimated at 2,000 head, with week to date movement of about 64,500.
Packer demand faded after midday, suggesting they had enough cattle booked for early next week, the sources said.
Beef movement remained strong at midday, but at sharply discounted prices, which could lead to lower packer bids for fed cattle on Thursday, market sources said.
Beef prices Wednesday were quoted $0.83 to $1.07 per cwt lower, with 323 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Prices were discounted amid increased beef tonnage from this week's heavy slaughter pace, the sources said.
Cattle slaughter on Wednesday was estimated at 134,000 head, which brought the weekly figure to 398,000 head, compared with 386,000 a week ago and 397,000 a year ago, USDA said.
